extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community — grant applicants, investigators, administrators, and institutional officials
extracted.subtask_description: Collection of NIH news items summarizing recent policy, process, and resource updates relevant to preparing and managing NIH grant applications and awards (e.g., model selection, data management plans, replication/reproducibility, peer review changes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting research models / New Approach Methodologies (NAMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance understanding of human health and disease; investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential when appropriate; select model systems that are scientifically justified and align with the research question. (Original phrasing: "NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches... investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions.")

rubrics_metrics.name: PF5 Collaborative International Research Projects — follow application format and key features
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants for NIH’s Collaborative International Research Projects (PF5) should learn the award structure, key features, and the required application format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch NIH’s 6-minute overview to learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests. Be prepared that an application could be split into linked awards during administrative processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH issued a new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing DMS Plans for applicable applications, use the 2026 Pilot format and include the simplified required elements as specified by NIH. This is the current required format for the pilot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed replication and reproducibility in applications and awards
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH emphasizes reliability of biomedical research and encourages a culture that values replication and reproducibility across the research enterprise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate replication and reproducibility considerations into study design, applications, and award planning. NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan and the Replication and Reproducibility Initiative are intended to drive, incentivize, and institutionalize replication and reproducibility efforts; expect these to be a highlighted topic in relevant guidance and reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand "Competitive But Not Discussed" review designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Following emergency modifications, NIH designated the middle third of applications in a study section as "competitive but not discussed" recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should understand that being scored in the middle third makes an application 'competitive but not discussed' — it may be considered competitive despite not being discussed in the study section. This affects expectations about discussion, score interpretation, and downstream actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized peer review — process change and implications
rubrics_metrics.description: As of March 2025, NIH centralized all peer review within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and institutions should be aware that peer review has been consolidated to CSR and that this consolidation aims to strengthen efficiency, competition, and transparency; anticipate procedural and potentially substantive effects on review timelines and processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor NIH Data Book and other NIH resources for updates
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH Data Book FY updates and other resources (videos, highlighted topics, policy notices) are periodically updated and roll out new information important for applicants and awardees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularly consult NIH resources (Extramural Nexus, Data Book, Guide Notices) to stay current on policy changes, data updates, and resource releases that can affect application strategy and compliance.
